outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that on Sunday, Nov 15, hourly rolling blackouts of 1 to 2 queues for all consumers, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect around the clock in parts of Ukraine, eased from Saturday's 1.5 to 3 queues. UNN, citing Ukrenergo, previously said one queue is four hours; the Sunday notice did not restate queue length. No later official Sunday schedule change was found. New overnight outages: DTEK said a Russian attack on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 households in the Odesa region without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said crews began work once it was safe, that they were clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment, and that restoration will take time). Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, also said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility; Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk, and reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found. Prior Saturday outages with no later official restoration notice found: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on one of its facilities in the north of Odesa region on the morning of Nov 14 left almost 50,000 customers without power (no restoration time given; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly and that air-raid alerts were complicating the work). As of 5:30 p.m. EET Saturday, Sumyoblenergo said emergency restoration was still underway in part of Sumy region after a large-scale morning outage, and that repeated outages were possible during the work (no customer count released for security reasons). DTEK said Saturday morning that emergency cuts were in effect in the Bucha, Fastiv, and Obukhiv districts of Kyiv region, with stabilization schedules in Kyiv city and the rest of the region. Poltava regional authorities said Saturday that bad weather left about 2,000 subscribers in 13 settlements without power. On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found.

outages.affected: Almost 50,000 customers without power, according to DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. Crews began work once it was safe, clearing rubble and repairing damaged equipment; DTEK said the facility had been hit repeatedly, that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work, and that restoration will take time. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found for this Nov 14 outage.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns (Santa Cruz unit 1, Antonio Guiteras, Felton unit 2, and Renté unit 6) and maintenance (Santa Cruz unit 3, Nuevitas unit 5, Felton unit 1, and Renté unit 5); thermal generation is also limited by 283 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Saturday bulletin forecast 1,860 MW affected at the evening peak: 970 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,830 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Saturday, the grid had 920 MW available versus 2,222 MW of demand, leaving 1,301 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,450 MW affected at midday. On Friday, service was affected all 24 hours, with a maximum of 1,912 MW at 6:20 p.m. UNE said Renté unit 6 was expected to add 50 MW at the Saturday evening peak. No official Saturday evening-peak actual was found, and CiberCuba's archive of official SEN bulletins still listed the Saturday bulletin as the latest; no Sunday UNE national bulletin had been published as of CiberCuba's 6:15 a.m. Cuba time Sunday update. On Sunday morning, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana reported generation-deficit outages of 236 MW on 101 distribution circuits at 6:00 a.m. Cuba time, after 118 circuits and 264 MW at 3:05 a.m.; it also reported some circuits restored and others newly affected. Empresa Eléctrica Villa Clara also reported affected circuits. The national grid was not reported as collapsed.

outages.cause: National generation shortfall during evening peak; Tarbela hydropower about 800 MW below normal after reduced water releases following the fifth-extension incident, plus seasonal hydrology and LNG limits
outages.affected: About 1,500 MW national shortfall during evening peak on Nov 11 (peak demand about 16,000 MW vs. about 14,500 MW available), according to ISMO figures cited Nov 12. ISMO said the Nov 10 shortfall, which reached about 2,530 MW, had eased and that generation was back to the routine plan as of Nov 11, but the 1,500 MW evening-peak gap (5 p.m. to 11 p.m.) remained. Discos were following existing 1.5 to 2 hour load-management schedules; The Nation reported some areas still facing up to five hours of additional load-shedding. No later official national ISMO update was found. On Saturday, Nov 14, HESCO spokesman Sadiq Kubar said the Hyderabad utility was receiving 565 MW from the national grid against demand of 1,034 MW, a shortfall of up to 469 MW, and was carrying out an additional 2 hours of load shedding across many feeders until required supply resumed. No customer count was given.
outages.updated: Nov 12, 2026 (ISMO / The Nation); HESCO Saturday statement (UrduPoint / APP, published 9:35 p.m. PKT = 10:35 a.m. CT); rechecked 5:57 AM CT Sunday, Nov 15, no later official national ISMO update found

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Homestead Park, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation and stabilise the network after the prolonged outage. The shutdown would affect customers restored during Phase 1, including the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West. City Power also said Sentech would remain without electricity until multiple cable faults had been located and repaired. No later official notice confirming the shutdown had ended, or giving a new customer count, was found. Earlier Saturday, City Power had restored electricity to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and residential customers in Mayfair West after overnight repairs and testing at the Hursthill and Mayfair substations, and said engineers would continue preparing for Phase 2, expected to restore remaining affected customers if there were no further technical challenges. No official Phase 2 completion notice was found. In a Saturday afternoon SABC report, City Power's Noel Maso said parts of Mayfair, Auckland Park, Crown Mines, and Vrededorp remained without power, that restoration and replacement costs stood at R24.8 million, and that in a worst-case scenario it could take up to 14 days to restore power to all affected areas. Maso also said a fault at Crown Substation was interrupting supply to Mayfair, Crown Mines, Amalgam, and surrounding communities, and that the Sentech Tower in Brixton was affected, with normal supply then set to be restored by Sunday; no later official confirmation that the Crown Substation fault had been cleared was found. City Power's 7:50 a.m. SAST Sunday Hursthill SDC bulletin said the centre was managing 1,384 open calls, 1,183 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). On Sunday afternoon, City Power said power had been restored in Victory Park (Parkhurst Substation; faulty cable reported Nov 14). At Roosevelt Substation, it said power in parts of Emmarentia (along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield) and Greenside had been partially restored, then that the fault had been located and jointing and termination would commence. Separately, City Power said a 33 kV cable was cut and stolen at Florida Glen Substation early Saturday, leaving customers in Florida Glen, Quellerina, Industria North, Bergbron, and Northcliff Ext 19 without power; replacement cable was expected on site Sunday, Nov 15, and no customer count or restoration time was given. No later official Sunday confirmation that the cable had arrived or that supply had returned was found. For Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia, City Power said at 12:10 p.m. SAST Sunday that power had been restored to Florida Substation except for 3 load centres affected by a burnt mini-substation and attempted vandalism, with the team sourcing materials for repairs; no customer count or restoration time was given for those remaining load centres.
outages.etr: City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown at Mayfair Substation would run from 12:00 noon Sunday, Nov 15 (SAST), affecting Phase 1 customers including Mayfair West, the SABC, and Netcare Garden City Hospital. It gave no separate restoration time for remaining unrestored Mayfair-area customers or for Sentech, which it said would stay off until multiple cable faults were located and repaired. For the Florida Glen cable-theft outage, replacement cable was expected on site Sunday, with no restoration time given. For the three remaining Florida Substation load centres, no restoration time was given

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 5:57 AM CT
